overlays.note: naust (boat-shed), NW corner — nothing ignites here; vocabulary planted for ch1-02

enemies.grid_notes: Boat-steerer of a hungry post-ban crew; holds the landing at beach centre beside the beached boat (surf line, elev 0) and routs W when half the crew falls.
Starts on the foot of the switchback road ([3,2], elev 0) and takes it — demonstrates the single-step 0→4 ascent along rows 2→1→0.

Charges due east at the naust and stalls at the 2h lip ([4,6] elev 0 vs [5,6] elev 2) — demonstrates Jump limits (C-ELEV-02: 2h faces are walls to Jump 2). The naust's whole west face ([5,5]-[5,7] over col 4) is a uniform 2h step; his nearest ways up are detours — e5's skerry stepping-stone stair [4,8]→[5,8] to the south, or the grass terraces to the north.

Enemy bow on the grounded skerry SW ([3,8], elev 1): 1h is not enough against the crag (elev 5) — the player's archer above out-ranges him by +2, making the 2h-per-+1 range rule legible from both sides.
South shingle; flanks north over the skerry stepping-stones (elev 1) onto the naust terrace (elev 2) — the witness pressure that teaches bodyguarding.

neutrals.grid_notes: Fisher-wife at the naust doorway on the naust terrace (elev 2); bolts north — a 1h drop to [5,4] — for the switchback and the rim when blades come out.
Old net-mender among the herring-racks on the second terrace (elev 3); slow, high, sees everything. The battle's default singer.
A loose goat on the grass terrace below the racks; its flight line east crosses the switchback choke ([7,2]-[8,0]) and blocks one road tile at the worst moment. Tutorial charm.

objectives.primary: Drive the raiders from the hold — fell or rout all five.
secondary: Down a raider with a bow shot fired from elevation 3+ (the range lesson, rewarded).

triggers.note: First sight of the descent-that-looks-like-ascent. Played absolutely straight; doctrine is fact in Ch1 (C-LIE-01).
Rout preview: surviving raiders flee W to the boat. Routers who escape make the battle Sung (C-ALIGN-04) — surfaced in the post-battle ledger card.
UI beat: back-attack bonus called out on e2 (C-FACE-01).

designer_notes.height_gimmick: A one-way amphitheatre fought from the top down: the defenders (player) begin holding ALL the height — deployment on the rim plateau (cols 9-11, elev 4-5) and the crag lip (col 8, elev 5) — and the raiders must climb into bow-fire, so the tutorial lesson is spending elevation. Every 2h of advantage buys +1 bow range over the beach (C-ELEV-01): the crag archer at elev 5 shoots +2 over shingle at 0 and over the skerry bow at 1, and neither can answer. The north switchback road (rows 2→1→0, elev 0,1,1,2,2 then 3,3 then 4,4) is the ONLY 0-to-4 ascent in single steps; the face below the rim (col 7 elev 3 vs col 8 elev 5, and the north shoulder at 4 over slopes 1-2) jumps 2-4h per tile and is unclimbable for Jump 2 — so the only path down into melee gives all of it back, and no other Ch1 map starts the player rich in height and teaches its exchange rate.
designer_notes.witness_setup: Two hold-folk shelter in the raiders' path and see everything: n1 the fisher-wife at the naust doorway ([5,5], elev 2) and n2 the old net-mender among the herring-racks ([7,4], elev 3); a loose goat (n3) adds flight-line comedy on the road choke. e5 flanks over the skerry stepping-stones straight at them. Beaten raiders can rout west to their beached boat (escape edge W). This battle is meant to be Sung — it is the player's own hearth and the witnesses are their own people; keeping it Unsung would require letting or making the hold's folk die, which the game permits and remembers (C-ALIGN-03). Teaches the witness/ledger UI in its gentlest case.
designer_notes.intent: Tutorial: movement, CT turn order, facing basics, elevation and bow range, first valkyrie VFX on a downed unit (the Harvest Lie shown as beautiful fact, C-LIE-01/C-DEATH-01). Enemy count and levels forgiving; defeat unlikely. The winter sea (cols 0-1) is water_deep and therefore intrinsically drowning-lethal — the downward pull is the terrain itself, no drown_edge overlays needed (D-TERR-02).
